meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm here about Owen's zero. Who decided on it, and did anyone speak to him first?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Go on.

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. A paste from his own notes would look the same, so what in that history says otherwise? And under your own procedure, was Owen asked about it before the zero went in?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
That history doesn't change what I want: this stays off his record, and it stays quiet. What else do you have?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
I've looked, and I don't see it. But students misquote from memory all the time, so what does that prove beyond a wrong line?
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Fine. I'm not arguing the line. What are you actually putting in front of me?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their minds between an outline and an essay; that's what drafting is. Is there a document that says otherwise?

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Okay. A private rewrite before December 1, its mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record. I'll take that to put this behind him, and I want it in writing tonight.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Thursday the twelfth works. Put the date, the time and the room in the email tonight, along with the rest.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4 on Thursday the twelfth after school, before December 1, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still want the time and the room, and all of it confirmed in writing. I expect that email tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: Her last position: she accepted the private supervised rewrite on Thursday the twelfth, before December 1, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, and she still wants the time, the room and all of it in writing tonight; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time did not run out first.
What moved her: You turned the play open to the scene and told her to search it herself, which gave her a check she could make on her own and left her only a weak defence.
What cost ground: Nothing; you owned the zero in your first sentence, kept the detector out of it, and never accused Owen.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM, saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, watched Owen close it, and never asked; your version history with its late-night times on October 28 came close to that night, which is why her answers got shorter, but it proves nothing about the essay and it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she said students change their minds between an outline and an essay, you moved straight to the offer, so answer that defence first, for example by showing what in the outline's reasoning carries into the essay.
